## Beam Buying Guide

### How do I measure for a ceiling beam or a mantel?
For a ceiling beam, measure the length the beam should cover, and note the ceiling height and which way the joists run. Solid and box beams come in 8, 12, 16, and 20 ft lengths, and other lengths are available by quote. For a mantel, measure the fireplace opening and the overhang you want on each side; stock mantels have an 8 inch face, are 10 inches deep, and run 6 to 10 ft. Send those measurements with the free quote form so we can price the length you need.

### Should I choose a box beam or a solid beam?
Choose a box beam if you want the look of a timber on a finished ceiling and you need something much lighter than solid wood. A box beam is a three-sided hollow beam, open on top, so it slides over a mounting board. A solid beam is 8 by 8 or 10 by 10 inches and it's heavy, so plan for proper support and a carpenter or builder to install it. Both are decorative unless your builder or a structural engineer approves the piece to carry a load.

### How are beams mounted?
Box beams are usually mounted by screwing a wood board, called blocking, into the ceiling joists, then sliding the beam over it and fastening through the sides. Mantels are usually hung on a hidden steel bracket or on lag bolts set into studs or masonry. Solid beams are heavy, so plan the support before they go up. We recommend a carpenter or builder for the install.

### How do I pick a stain to match my floors or cabinets?
Beams, mantels, and tables come in a natural (clear), medium, or dark finish. Hold a sample of your floor or cabinet color next to those three and pick the closest one. Reclaimed wood won't match another finish exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. If you're between two tones, describe the floors and cabinets on the free quote form and tell us which finish you want.

### How long does a custom order take, and how does a quote work?
Every piece is made to order, so the timing depends on the size and the wood available, and we give you an estimated time with your quote. Use the free quote form, or call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), and tell us the piece, the size, the finish, and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the price and shipping, and you're under no obligation. Once you approve the quote, you can pay securely online by card, and we send photos before your piece ships.

### Do you ship beams, and how are they packed?
Yes, we ship to every state in the continental US by freight or ground carrier, depending on size and weight, and each piece is packed with care. Shipping is quoted to your ZIP code before you pay. Put your ZIP on the free quote form and the shipping price comes back with the wood price.

### How do I clean and care for a hand-hewn beam?
Dust the beam with a soft, dry cloth, and wipe spills promptly so water doesn't sit on the wood. Don't soak the beam or use harsh cleaners, because they can dull a natural, medium, or dark finish. The adze marks, nail holes, and weathered color are part of the wood, so clean the surface and leave the texture as it is. If you have a question about the finish after it arrives, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326) or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to.

### Can I get a table that matches my beams?
Yes, we make dining, coffee, and console tables to order from the same hand-hewn reclaimed beams, in a natural, medium, or dark finish. Tell us the size, the finish, and your room, and mention any mantel or ceiling beams you want it to sit with. No two pieces of reclaimed wood match exactly. We'll send a free quote with shipping to your ZIP code.

## Fireplace mantel sizing guide

How to size a reclaimed wood fireplace mantel: measure the firebox, add overhang, then match a stock length. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-guide

### How do I size a reclaimed wood fireplace mantel?
Measure the width of the firebox opening in inches, then add 6 to 12 inches of overhang on each side. That total is the mantel length. Stock mantels from Barndo Beam Co. have an 8 inch face, are 10 inches deep, and come in 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 ft lengths, from about $1,050. If the math lands between stock lengths, round up to the next length, or request a custom length. The shortest stock mantel is 6 ft, so a smaller firebox simply gets a little more overhang. Send the firebox width, the length, the finish, and your ZIP code with a free quote for the wood price and shipping.

### How much should a fireplace mantel overhang the firebox?
Add 6 to 12 inches of overhang on each side of the firebox opening. Six inches looks tighter. Twelve inches looks heavier and suits a thick reclaimed beam. A 48 inch firebox plus 12 inches on each side is 72 inches, which is a 6 ft mantel. A 60 inch firebox plus 12 inches on each side is 84 inches, which is a 7 ft mantel. A 36 inch firebox is shorter than the 6 ft stock minimum, so a 6 ft mantel leaves about 18 inches of overhang on each side. Measure the firebox opening, inside edge to inside edge.

### Should I choose a mantel beam or a full fireplace surround?
Choose a mantel beam when you only need the shelf across the top. A stock mantel is 8 inches tall by 10 inches deep, in 6 to 10 ft lengths. Choose a one-of-a-kind mantel beam when you want to approve photos of one exact beam before it is cut. The face is usually 8 to 10 inches, and lengths start at 6 ft. Choose a full beam fireplace surround when you want a mantel plus two legs, three matching beams that frame the opening. Surrounds are available, and custom sizes are quoted. Finishes are natural (clear), medium, or dark. Request a free quote with your ZIP code and we reply within 2 business days with the price and shipping.

### What stock mantel sizes are available?
Stock reclaimed wood mantels have an 8 inch tall face and are 10 inches deep. Lengths are 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 ft, and a 6 ft mantel starts at about $1,050. Lengths longer than 10 ft are available by quote. A full beam fireplace surround, a mantel plus two legs, is available too. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide. Finishes are natural (clear), medium, or dark.

## Dining table sizing guide

How to size a custom reclaimed wood dining table: match seats to a length, pick a width and a base, then request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#table-guide

### How do I size a custom reclaimed wood dining table?
Count the seats, then match a length. Allow about 24 inches of table length per person. A custom reclaimed wood dining table from Barndo Beam Co. is usually 36 inches (3 ft) or 42 inches (3.5 ft) wide. Four seats fit a 5 or 6 ft table. Six seats fit a 6 or 7 ft table. Eight seats fit an 8 ft table. Ten seats fit a 10 ft table. Twelve seats fit a 12 ft table. Rectangular farmhouse tables run 5 to 12 ft, from about $3,150. Choose a trestle, beam legs, or a beam top on steel, then a natural, medium, or dark finish. Send the seat count, the length, the width, the base, the finish, and your ZIP code with a free quote. Every table is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

### How long should a reclaimed wood dining table be for 4, 6, 8, 10, or 12 people?
Allow about 24 inches of length per person. Four people fit a 5 or 6 ft table. Six people fit a 6 or 7 ft table. Eight people fit an 8 ft table. Ten people fit a 10 ft table. Twelve people fit a 12 ft table. Barndo Beam Co. builds rectangular reclaimed wood dining tables in those lengths, 36 or 42 inches wide, handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

### How wide should a custom dining table be?
A rectangular reclaimed wood dining table is usually 36 inches (3 ft) or 42 inches (3.5 ft) wide. Thirty-six inches seats one person on each side. Forty-two inches leaves room for serving dishes down the center. Leave about 36 inches of walkway behind each chair. Round and square tables from Barndo Beam Co. run 3 to 7 ft across.

### What is the difference between a trestle, beam legs, and a beam top on steel?
A trestle has two end supports joined by a stretcher, so chairs slide in along the sides. Beam legs are thick hand-hewn posts, the same timber face as a mantel. A beam top on steel keeps the reclaimed wood top and uses a black steel base. Barndo Beam Co. builds all three to order. Tell us which base you want when you request a free quote.

### How do I match a dining table to my existing beams or mantel?
Order the table in the same finish as the beams or mantel: natural (clear), medium, or dark. The table is built from the same hand-hewn reclaimed wood. No two pieces match exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. Name the mantel or beam finish on the free quote form, and we send photos of your table before it ships.

We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free, and every table is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

A custom reclaimed wood coffee table is usually about 16 to 18 inches tall, level with the sofa seat or an inch or two lower. Make the length about one-half to two-thirds of the sofa, and leave 12 to 18 inches of walkway on the open sides. ### How tall should a reclaimed wood coffee table be next to a sofa?
A reclaimed wood coffee table is usually about 16 to 18 inches tall, level with the sofa seat or an inch or two lower. Measure from the floor to the top of the seat cushion and set the table at that height or slightly under it. An 8 ft sofa pairs with a table about 48 to 64 inches long. Leave 12 to 18 inches of walkway between the table and the sofa, and on any side people walk past. Stock coffee tables from Barndo Beam Co. are 2 x 3, 2 x 4, 3 x 4, 3 x 5, 3 x 6, 4 x 6, 4 x 7, and 5 x 8 ft.

The stock height is 32 inches. A shelf under the top is available by quote. Request a free quote with your ZIP code.

## Ceiling beam sizing and spacing guide

How to size and space decorative ceiling beams: match the face to the ceiling height and the span, set the on-center spacing, count the beams, then request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide

### What size ceiling beam should I use for my ceiling height and room width?
Match the face of a decorative ceiling beam to the ceiling height, then to the span. On a ceiling about 8 to 9 feet high, an 8 by 8 inch beam is the stock solid size. On a ceiling about 9 to 12 feet high, 8 by 8 is the usual size. On a ceiling about 12 feet or taller, or across a wide great room, use a 10 by 10. For the span the beam crosses, an 8 by 8 suits a run up to about 16 ft, and a 10 by 10 suits a run of about 18 to 20 ft. Stock solid and box beams from Barndo Beam Co. come in 8, 12, 16, and 20 ft lengths. Space the beams about 3, 4, or 6 feet on center. A face larger than 10 by 10, or another length, is available by quote. These sizes are for a decorative beam. If the beam has to carry a load, have your builder or a structural engineer approve it first. Send the ceiling height, the room size, the beam count, solid or box, the finish, and your ZIP code with a free quote. Every beam is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

### How far apart should decorative ceiling beams be spaced?
Space decorative ceiling beams about 3, 4, or 6 feet on center. On center means from the center of one beam to the center of the next. About 3 feet on center is a tighter rhythm, and it suits a kitchen. About 4 feet on center is the usual spacing in a living room or great room with 8 by 8 beams. About 6 feet on center is a more open ceiling, and it pairs well with a 10 by 10 so each beam still reads. To space them evenly, divide the width you are spacing across by the number of beams. That result is the on-center spacing, and the center of the first and last beam sits half of that spacing in from each side wall. A room 12 ft across with 3 beams is 4 ft on center. A room 16 ft across with 4 beams is 4 ft on center. A room 20 ft across with 5 beams is 4 ft on center.

### How many ceiling beams do I need for a common room?
Run the beams the long way and space them across the short way. A 12 by 12 ft room takes 3 beams, each 12 ft, at 4 ft on center. A matched package of 3 beams by 12 ft is $5,400, and a single solid 12 ft beam is $1,920. A 12 by 16 ft room takes 3 beams, each 16 ft, spaced across the 12 ft side at 4 ft on center. A matched package of 3 beams by 16 ft is $7,200. A 16 by 20 ft room takes 4 beams, each 20 ft, spaced across the 16 ft side at 4 ft on center. A solid 20 ft beam is $3,200, and a box beam at 20 ft is $3,300. A room 20 ft across takes 5 beams at 4 ft on center. A matched package of 5 beams by 20 ft is $15,000. Packages are matched for color and texture, 8 by 8 standard, at $150 per foot. Send the room size and your ZIP code with a free quote.

### Should I choose a solid hand-hewn beam or a hollow box beam for a ceiling?
Choose a solid hand-hewn beam when you want a full timber, 8 by 8 or 10 by 10 inches. It is solid wood and heavy, so plan the support with a carpenter or builder before it goes up. A solid beam is $1,280 at 8 ft, $1,920 at 12 ft, $2,560 at 16 ft, and $3,200 at 20 ft. Choose a box beam when you want the look of a timber on a finished ceiling and you need something much lighter. A box beam is a three-sided hollow beam, open on top, so it slides over a wood mounting board screwed into the joists, then fastens through the sides. A box beam is $1,320 at 8 ft, $1,980 at 12 ft, $2,640 at 16 ft, and $3,300 at 20 ft. Custom widths are by quote, which helps on a lower ceiling. Both are decorative unless your builder or a structural engineer approves the piece to carry a load.

### Which finish should I choose for ceiling beams?
Ceiling beams come in a natural (clear), medium, or dark finish, the same three finishes as mantels and tables. Natural keeps the weathered color of the reclaimed wood. Medium warms it. Dark deepens the grain and sits well with black window frames and iron. Hold a sample of your floor or cabinet color next to those three and pick the closest one. Reclaimed wood won't match another finish exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. Name the finish on the free quote form, and we send photos before the beams ship.

### How do I measure for ceiling beams?
Measure the ceiling height from the finished floor to the finished ceiling. Measure the span each beam will cover, wall to wall, in the direction the beams will run. That number is the beam length. Measure the other direction, the width you will space the beams across. Note which way the joists run. Beams usually run across the joists so the mounting board can fasten into them. Note lights, fans, and soffits the beams have to clear. Stock lengths are 8, 12, 16, and 20 ft. If the span falls between those, round up to the next stock length or ask for a custom length. Send the height, the length, the width, the beam count, and your ZIP code with a free quote.

### How do I request a free quote for ceiling beams?
Use the free quote form, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Include the ceiling height, the beam length, the width you are spacing across, the beam count, the on-center spacing, solid or box, the size (8 by 8 or 10 by 10), the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free, and every beam is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

## Reclaimed beam care and finish guide

How to clean, finish, and care for a hand-hewn reclaimed beam, mantel, or beam table top: dust it dry, pick a finish, leave normal checks, keep it out of direct weather, follow the fireplace maker's mantel clearance, and request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide

### How do I clean and dust a hand-hewn reclaimed beam or mantel?
Dust a hand-hewn reclaimed beam or mantel with a soft, dry cloth, a lambswool duster, or a vacuum with a soft brush on low. Work along the grain. The adze marks, nail holes, and weathered color are part of the wood, so clean the surface and leave the texture. For a fingerprint or a light mark, wipe with a barely damp cloth and dry the spot at once. Do not soak the beam. Do not use a steam mop, bleach, ammonia, or a harsh cleaner, because they can dull a natural, medium, or dark finish. Do not sand the face. Sanding removes the hand-hewn marks.

### What is the difference between a raw beam, a clear matte sealer, an oil finish, and a light stain?
A raw beam has no film on the wood. You see the weathered gray-brown, the checks, and the tool marks, and water can spot it. A clear matte sealer is a thin clear coat with almost no shine, so the color stays close to the raw beam and a spill beads instead of soaking in at once. That is the look of a natural (clear) finish. An oil soaks in, deepens the amber and the grain, and stays low in sheen. It is not a hard film, and an oiled top can take a thin coat again later. A light stain is a thin warm tint, lighter than a medium or dark stain, and the checks and adze marks still show. Beams, mantels, and tables from Barndo Beam Co. are finished natural (clear), medium, or dark before they ship. Natural is the clear look. Medium warms the wood. Dark deepens the grain. Name the finish on the free quote form. Reclaimed wood will not match another finish exactly.

### Are checks and cracks normal in old reclaimed wood?
Yes. A check is a split that follows the grain. Old hand-hewn beams checked as they dried, often decades ago, and a check, a nail hole, or a small crack in the face is normal in reclaimed wood. It does not mean a decorative beam is failing. Wood also moves a little when indoor humidity changes, so a hairline check can open in the first heating season. Leave the checks. Filler can pop out when the wood moves. If a piece arrives broken, or a crack runs across the beam rather than along the grain, send photos within 48 hours to barndobeamco@agentmail.to or call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326).

### Can I use a reclaimed beam indoors or on a covered porch?
Use a reclaimed beam indoors, or on a covered porch where the roof keeps rain off it. A porch or entry header is for that covered spot. Keep the beam out of direct weather. Do not set it where rain, a sprinkler, or standing water hits the wood. Direct weather swells the beam, opens checks, and wears a finish off. Indoors, dust the beam and keep standing water off it. Every beam is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

### How much heat clearance does a wood fireplace mantel need?
Follow your local building code and the clearance listed by the fireplace maker. A wood mantel is combustible. The safe distance from the firebox opening to the wood is set by that listing and by local code. Read the fireplace manual, and have the installer confirm the mantel height before the beam goes up. If the listing is missing, do not guess. Ask the installer or the local building office. Barndo Beam Co. supplies the wood mantel. The fireplace maker's clearance is the one to follow.

### How do I care for a reclaimed beam table top?
Use coasters under glasses, bottles, and plants. Wipe a spill right away, especially water, wine, or oil, then dry the spot. Do not set a hot pan on the wood, and do not use a soaking cloth. On an oiled top, re-oil when water stops beading or the surface looks dry: wipe on a thin coat, let it soak in, and wipe off all of the extra oil. On a clear sealed top, or a bar top with a sealed bar finish, dust and wipe. Do not strip a sealer to re-oil it. Tell us if the top is for dining when you request a free quote, and include your ZIP code.

### How do I request a free quote for a beam, mantel, or beam table?
Use the free quote form, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Tell us the piece (a ceiling beam, a mantel, a porch header, or a table), the size, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide, across the continental United States.

## Mantel install guide

How to install a reclaimed beam mantel: find the studs or solid masonry, check that the wall is level, set the height from local building code and the fireplace or insert manufacturer, choose a hidden steel bracket, a cleat lagged into studs, or masonry anchors, plan for the weight of a solid beam, and request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-install-guide

### What are the common ways to mount a reclaimed beam mantel?
Three mounts are common. A hidden steel bracket, or steel rods, is drilled into the back of the beam so the hardware stays out of sight. A wood cleat is fastened with lag screws into the wall studs, and the mantel sits on that cleat. On a brick or stone fireplace, masonry anchors go into the solid masonry, not into drywall. Pick the mount that matches the wall. A carpenter should do the install. Barndo Beam Co. supplies the wood mantel, and the mantel is decorative.

### How do I find studs or blocking for a mantel?
Find the studs with a stud finder, then confirm each center. Studs are often 16 inches apart, and sometimes 24. Mark the centers where the mantel will sit. The fasteners have to land in studs or in solid wood blocking, not in drywall alone. If the studs miss the spots that need to carry the beam, a carpenter can add blocking. On a finished wall, line the bracket or the cleat up with the studs you found. Do not use drywall anchors for a solid beam.

### How do I check that the fireplace wall is level before I hang a mantel?
Hold a long level where the mantel will sit. Check side to side, so the shelf will be level, and check the wall face, so the beam will not tilt out at one end. Brick and stone are often uneven. Shim behind the cleat or the bracket so the mantel reads level even when the stone does not. Check the mantel with the level again before the last fasteners are tightened. Drill the holes in the back of the beam only after the height and the level are set.

### How heavy is a solid reclaimed beam mantel, and can the wall hold it?
A solid reclaimed mantel is real timber, not a hollow box. A longer beam weighs more than a shorter one, and a thicker beam weighs more than a thinner one. Plan on two or more people to lift it, and have a carpenter or builder do the install. The weight has to go into wall studs or into solid masonry. Drywall, a thin stone veneer that is only stuck to the wall, and plastic anchors are not the support. If you are not sure the wall can hold the beam, stop and ask a carpenter before you drill. Each reclaimed beam is a different piece of wood, so there is no single weight for every mantel. Ask for the weight of your beam on the free quote if your carpenter needs it, and include your ZIP code.

### How much clearance does a combustible mantel need above the firebox?
Clearance above the firebox for a combustible mantel is set by your local building code and by the fireplace or insert manufacturer. Check both. A wood mantel is combustible. Read the manual for that fireplace or insert, and confirm the clearance with the local building office or your installer. If the manual and the local code do not match, follow the stricter one. Do not copy a height from a photo, and do not guess a number. Set the mantel height only after that clearance is known. Barndo Beam Co. supplies the wood mantel. The code and the fireplace maker set the clearance.

### Should a homeowner install a reclaimed beam mantel?
A homeowner can plan the job: find the studs, check that the wall is level, read the fireplace or insert manual, and check local building code. Hanging the beam is a carpenter's job on most walls, because a solid beam is heavy and the fasteners have to hit studs or solid masonry. If the fireplace is an insert, follow that manufacturer's instructions as well as local code. We recommend a carpenter or builder for the install.

### How do I request a free quote for a reclaimed wood mantel?
Use the free quote form, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Tell us the mantel length, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), whether the wall is framed, brick, or stone, and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free. Every mantel is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

## Holiday mantel styling guide

How to decorate a reclaimed beam mantel for the holidays: layer greenery, candles, and stockings, hang stockings with weighted holders so the wood stays unmarked, keep flammables away from a working fireplace, follow the fireplace manufacturer and local code, and request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#holiday-mantel-guide

### How do I decorate a reclaimed beam mantel for the holidays?
Layer a reclaimed beam mantel from the wall outward. Set garland or greenery along the back of the shelf so it does not drape into the firebox. Place candles or small objects in front of the greenery, and hang stockings off the front edge. Leave the center of the firebox clear. A stock mantel is 10 inches deep, so plan one row, not a deep display. Use battery candles on the wood. If you use real candles, keep them in sturdy holders, keep them off the greenery, and never leave them burning unattended. Keep every flammable away from the fire, and follow the fireplace or insert manufacturer and your local code. Do not guess a clearance number. Every mantel from Barndo Beam Co. is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

### How do I hang stockings on a solid wood beam mantel without damaging it?
Use weighted stocking holders. The weight sits on the shelf and the hook drops over the front edge, so you do not drill the beam. Set the weight toward the back of the 10 inch shelf so a full stocking does not tip the holder. Hang the stockings beside the firebox opening, not across it, and keep them clear of candles and greenery. A small screw hook or nail leaves a hole that stays. If you use a small hook, put it on the underside near the front edge, and keep it off the hand-hewn face. Do not drill the back of the beam where a hidden bracket or rods may already sit. Skip adhesive hooks. They can pull a natural, medium, or dark finish off when you remove them. After the holidays, lift the weighted holders off and the wood is unchanged.

### How much clearance do candles and greenery need from a working fireplace?
Keep flammables away from a working fireplace and away from any flame. Greenery, dried branches, ribbons, paper, and stockings can burn, and a wood mantel is combustible too. The safe distance from the firebox opening to the wood is set by your local building code and by the fireplace or insert manufacturer. Decorations follow that same rule. Do not hang greenery, a stocking, or a ribbon into the firebox or into the clearance the manual requires. Do not guess a number of inches, and do not copy a distance from a photo. Read the fireplace or insert manual, and follow local code. If they do not match, follow the stricter one. Battery candles remove the open flame from the shelf. If you burn the fireplace, keep the mantel clear of anything that can fall, swing, or drip into the opening, and do not leave real candles lit. Barndo Beam Co. supplies the wood mantel. The fireplace maker and local code set the clearance.

### How do I choose mantel length and depth before the holidays?
Measure the firebox opening, inside edge to inside edge, then add 6 to 12 inches of overhang on each side. That total is the mantel length. The overhang is where the end stockings hang, so they sit beside the opening instead of across it. Stock mantels from Barndo Beam Co. have an 8 inch tall face and are 10 inches deep, in 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 ft lengths. Ten inches of depth holds one layer of garland plus stocking holders. If the math lands between stock lengths, round up to the next length, or ask for a custom length. A deeper shelf is a custom size by quote. The wood still has to clear the firebox by whatever your local code and the fireplace maker require. See how to size a reclaimed wood fireplace mantel at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-guide and how to install a reclaimed beam mantel at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-install-guide.

### When should I order a reclaimed wood mantel for the holidays?
Order early for the holidays. Every mantel is made to order, so the timing depends on the size and the wood available. Ask about current lead times in your free quote. The estimate comes back with the quote. This page does not promise a date. Send the mantel length, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. Every mantel is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

## Hand-hewn vs. resawn vs. faux beam guide

How to tell real reclaimed wood: read the face for adze or broad-axe marks, circular or band saw marks, or a faux beam of new lumber or foam, then check nail holes, mortise pockets, checks, patina, and weight. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#hewn-vs-faux-guide

### What does hand-hewn mean on a reclaimed wood beam?
Hand-hewn means the faces were shaped with an adze or a broad axe, not with a saw. An adze leaves short scooped cuts. A broad axe leaves longer facets. The cuts overlap and change direction, so the face is uneven, with high spots and low spots, and the edges wander. A hewn face does not show repeating circular arcs or straight parallel saw lines. The end of a beam is often sawn square when it is cut to length. Read the long faces, not that end cut.

### How is resawn or rough-sawn reclaimed wood different from hand-hewn?
Resawn wood is old timber cut again on a saw. Rough-sawn means the saw texture was left on the face instead of being planed smooth. A circular saw leaves repeating arcs across the face. A band saw leaves fine, fairly straight, parallel lines. The face is flatter and more even than a hand-hewn face. The timber can still be old. Nail holes, checks, and gray patina can remain on a surface that was not resawn, while the fresh-sawn face looks lighter and shows the saw pattern. Saw marks alone do not prove the wood is old.

### What do faux beams made of new lumber or foam look like?
A faux beam imitates a timber. A new-lumber box is flat boards joined into a U-shape or a hollow rectangle. The faces are flat, the edges are crisp and square, the grain looks new, and the stain is often one even brown. It has no old nail holes, mortise pockets, or deep checks, and it is much lighter than solid timber of the same outside size. Molded foam is lighter still. The texture can repeat, the color is paint on the surface, it sounds thin when tapped, and it can flex or dent. A hollow box can still be real reclaimed wood. A Barndo Beam Co. hand-hewn box beam is three-sided, made from reclaimed wood that still shows adze and axe marks, and it is not foam and not new lumber.

### What are the signs of real age in reclaimed wood?
Look for nail holes or spike holes, often with dark iron stain, and for mortise pockets, peg holes, or notches where the timber joined a frame. A check is a split that follows the grain, left as the beam dried. Patina is uneven gray, amber, and brown that sits down in the tool marks, not one even coat of stain on the surface. Weight is the other test. Solid old timber is heavy for its size. Foam of the same outside size is light, and a new-lumber box falls in between. Each reclaimed beam is different, so ask for the weight of the piece you are buying.

### Should I choose a hand-hewn beam, resawn reclaimed wood, or a faux beam for a mantel, ceiling, or table?
Choose hand-hewn reclaimed wood for a fireplace mantel, a feature ceiling beam, or a table people will touch. The uneven face and the axe marks hold up at close range. Solid beams are heavy, so plan support with a carpenter. Choose resawn or rough-sawn reclaimed wood when you want a flatter face for a table top or a straighter ceiling line, and confirm the timber is actually old. Choose a faux beam of new lumber or foam only for a lightweight decorative ceiling seen from across the room. It will not pass a close look on a mantel or a table. Barndo Beam Co. beams, mantels, and tables are hand-hewn reclaimed wood, handcrafted in Oklahoma, shipped in the continental US. They are decorative unless a builder or a structural engineer approves a piece to carry a load.

### What questions should I ask before I buy a reclaimed beam?
Ask whether the face was shaped with an adze or a broad axe, or cut on a circular saw or a band saw. Ask whether the piece is solid timber, a hollow box of reclaimed wood, a box of new lumber, or foam. Ask for close photos of the long face, the end, and any nail holes, mortise pockets, or checks. Ask whether the color is original patina or a stain on newer wood, and ask what the piece weighs. Ask whether it is sold as decorative. A beam that has to carry a load needs a builder or a structural engineer. Ask whether you will see photos of your exact piece before it ships.

## Beam ideas by room

Where hand-hewn reclaimed beams, mantels, and custom beam tables go in a great room, a kitchen, at a fireplace, in a dining room, in an entry or on a covered porch, and in a bedroom. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-ideas-by-room

### How are hand-hewn reclaimed beams used on a great room or living room ceiling?
Run the beams the long way of the room and leave a clear gap for the fan and the lights. A tall great room can take a larger face, and a lower living room ceiling usually wants fewer beams or hollow box beams. For the face, the count, and the spacing, see the ceiling beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide.

### How do I use reclaimed beams on a kitchen ceiling or around a range hood?
Set the ceiling beams across the kitchen and stop them short of the hood, or run them beside it, so the hood and the duct stay clear. Any wood near a working range has to sit outside the clearance the range and hood maker require, so do not guess that number. For spacing, see the ceiling beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide.

### Should a fireplace get one mantel beam or a mantel plus two legs?
Use one mantel beam when you only need the shelf, and add two legs when you want the opening framed in the same wood. Size the length from the firebox, and set the height only after you check local code and the fireplace or insert maker. See the mantel sizing guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-guide and the mantel install guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-install-guide.

### How do I use a beam table in a dining room that also has ceiling beams?
Center the beam table under the ceiling beams and order it in the same finish: natural, medium, or dark. Choose a trestle or beam-leg base when you want the wood to show, or a steel base when the ceiling is already full of timber. For seats, length, and width, see the dining table guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#table-guide.

### Can I use a reclaimed beam in an entryway or on a porch?
Use a beam console inside the entry, and use a porch header only under a roof that keeps rain off the wood. Do not set a beam where rain or a sprinkler hits it. For the console size, see the coffee and console guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#coffee-console-guide, and for weather and finish, see the beam care guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#beam-care-guide.

### How do I use a reclaimed beam in a bedroom?
Center one beam over the bed, running the width of the bed or a little past the nightstands, and keep it clear of the ceiling fan and the light. On a lower bedroom ceiling, a hollow box beam keeps the weight down and the face from crowding the bed. For solid versus box, see the ceiling beam guide at https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide.

Use the free quote form at https://barndobeamco.com/#quote, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to, and tell us the room, the piece, the size, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code.
